title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: UN Charter force prohibition
sections.summary: The UN Charter included articles prohibiting the use of force except in limited circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Charter of the United Nations (UN) included articles prohibiting the use of force, save in limited circumstances.

sections.label: GATT foundation for trade
sections.summary: In 1947 the GATT was entered into, laying the foundation for international trade and the WTO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Two years later in 1947, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was entered into, which laid the foundation for international trade and the World Trade Organization (WTO).

sections.label: Russia invasion violates UN Charter
sections.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine violates Article 24 of the UN Charter, but Russia's Security Council membership prevents a coordinated response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a direct violation of Article 24 of the UN Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, as Russia is a Security Council member of the UN, a coordinated response by the UN Security Council is not possible.

sections.label: Multilateral platforms effectiveness questioned
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether multinational platforms remain relevant, saying the WTO, WHO and UN have been helpless and ineffective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, are multinational platforms still relevant and effective in dealing with our global problems today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have seen our multilateral platforms like the WTO, World Health Organization (WHO) and UN being helpless and ineffective in dealing with crisis and resolving deep-seated global issues and very often end up just being a platform for grandstanding and rhetoric.

sections.label: US-China frictions pose risks
sections.summary: US-China frictions over trade, security and technology pose risks to global economic recovery and regional stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The grave frictions between the US and China over areas, such as trade, security and technology, pose risks to the fragile recovery in the global economy and to regional stability.

sections.label: Singapore ties with China, US
sections.summary: China and the US were among Singapore's top trading partners in 2021, and Singapore seeks an update on how their rivalry affects it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: China and the US were also among Singapore's top trading partners in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, besides being China's largest foreign investor since 2013, Singapore also has three high level government-to-government projects with China, including the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative launched in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: I would thus like to seek an update from MFA on how the continued rivalry between the world's two largest economies will affect Singapore.

sections.label: MFA COVID-19 efforts
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister how MFA has supported national and global efforts against COVID-19, noting other countries' situations affect Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This means that whatever the COVID-19 situation in other countries will, inevitably, affect Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Minister how has MFA supported the national and global efforts against COVID-19?

sections.label: MFA role in Ukraine
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MFA will play a further role in Ukraine, including facilitating Singaporeans' exit and Ukrainians' stay in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Does MFA see itself playing any further role in this issue, including facilitating the exit of Singaporeans from Ukraine, and/or facilitating the stay of the Ukrainians in Singapore, in the event something untoward happens and they are unable to return home?

sections.label: Singapore sanctions on Russia
sections.summary: The passage asks what else Singapore can do to garner support from other countries, especially ASEAN neighbours, to uphold international law and sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: As Singapore has already imposed sanctions on Russia, may I ask the Minister, what else can Singapore do to garner support from other countries and, in particular, our ASEAN neighbours, to have all our neighbours agree to uphold international law and to respect each country's sovereignty?

sections.label: Southeast Asia growth engine
sections.summary: The passage states Southeast Asia remains a key growth engine for Singapore due to its population, middle class, free trade commitment, and ASEAN Economic Community potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Thirdly, SEA remains a key engine of growth for Singapore because (a) SEA, collectively, has a large and relatively young population, as well as a large and growing middle class; (b) SEA remains committed to free trade and regional integration; and (c) the ASEAN Economic Community, which all SEA nations are part of, could rise from being the seventh-largest economy today to becoming the fourth largest by 2030.

sections.label: Singapore relations with Malaysia, Indonesia
sections.summary: The passage seeks an update on Singapore-Malaysia relations during COVID-19 and notes the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat milestones and agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I know our two governments have continued to work closely together and share a desire to gradually restore cross-border travel and resume other activities for the mutual benefit of both countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would thus like to seek an update on Singapore’s relations with one of our closest partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How has Singapore maintained our relations with Malaysia amidst the COVID-19 pandemic?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders’ Retreat held in Bintan on 25 January 2022 brought about significant milestones in the bilateral relations of our countries through an expanded framework of agreements in our Flight Information Regions, Defence Cooperation and the Extradition Treaty.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: MOUs on Green and Circular Economy Development and an MOU on Energy Cooperation were also signed between the two nations, with impact on green growth opportunities, low-carbon energy infrastructure, and development of new emerging green technology.

sections.label: Deferred VTLs launched
sections.summary: The passage states the Government launched deferred vaccinated travel lanes with the UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: More recently, the Government had moved to launch the deferred VTLs with the UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

sections.label: Singapore training Palestinian officials
sections.summary: Singapore trained over 500 Palestinian officials through ETAP and sponsored Palestinian students for post-graduate degrees locally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Minister for Foreign Affairs explained how the Government has, through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Programme (ETAP), trained over 500 Palestinian officials in public administration, economic and urban development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Singapore also sponsored Palestinian students to pursue post-graduate degrees in our local Universities.

sections.label: US withdrawal and conflict risk
sections.summary: US withdrawal from Afghanistan and statements on Ukraine suggest limited appetite for foreign conflicts, risking emboldened aggressors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The recent US withdrawal from Afghanistan as well as the strong statements ruling out military involvement in Ukraine seemed to suggest that its appetite for involvement in foreign conflicts is limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There is a risk that if the world perceives that the US and the major powers are less prepared to uphold law and order, then potential aggressors would be emboldened to act in violation of international law.

sections.label: Singapore assistance and US investment
sections.summary: Singapore offered military planes for Afghanistan evacuation, and the US remains Singapore's largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A recent example of how we have assisted in the area of security is our offer of military planes to help with evacuation efforts in Afghanistan last August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Economy-wise, the US remains, by far, consistently the largest foreign investor in Singapore.

sections.label: China-Singapore trade and investment
sections.summary: Since 2013, China has been Singapore's largest trading partner and Singapore China's largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Since 2013, China has been Singapore’s largest trading partner, and Singapore has been China’s largest foreign investor.

sections.label: Singapore-Australia leaders' meeting
sections.summary: In June last year, Singapore's Prime Minister hosted Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison at the 6th Singapore-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, in June last year, our Prime Minister hosted Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison at the 6th Singapore-Australia Annual Leaders’ Meeting in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore-Australia vaccine dose sharing
sections.summary: In August, Singapore and Australia agreed to a dose sharing arrangement of COVID-19 vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In August, Singapore and Australia agreed to a dose sharing arrangement of COVID-19 vaccines.

sections.label: Singapore-New Zealand Enhanced Partnership
sections.summary: Singapore and New Zealand upgraded relations to an Enhanced Partnership in 2019, with 26 initiatives across four pillars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: When New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern visited Singapore in 2019, we upgraded bilateral relations to an Enhanced Partnership (EP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have developed 26 bilateral cooperation initiatives across the EP’s four pillars: trade and economics; security and defence; science, technology and innovation; and people-to-people links.

sections.label: Staying relevant in global economy
sections.summary: Staying relevant to global corporates, markets, supply chains and financial networks creates jobs, growth and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the global economy, it is imperative that we stay relevant to global corporates, global markets, global supply chains, global financial networks, so as to create good jobs for our people, strong growth for our businesses and sustainability for our country.

sections.label: MFA assistance during pandemic
sections.summary: MFA faced unprecedented assistance requests and officers worked tirelessly to bring citizens home despite closed borders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: MFA had faced an unprecedented number of requests for assistance since the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: MFA officers worked tirelessly to bring our citizens home even when international borders were shut.

sections.label: MFA consular services and missions
sections.summary: MFA must keep consular services effective, and faces repatriation issues where it has no ground presence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: MFA must ensure their operational capabilities remain effective and meet Singaporeans' demand for prompt and effective consular services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What challenges does MFA face that require public support?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I also understand that MFA has over 50 overseas missions worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Despite this, we face issues relating to repatriation efforts during the pandemic as there are some Singaporeans located in countries where the Ministry has no ground presence.

sections.label: Singaporeans brought home
sections.summary: More than 4,600 Singaporeans who had difficulty returning were brought home in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I say that again, we left no Singaporean behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have helped to bring home more than 4,600 Singaporeans who had difficulty getting back for some reason or the another in the last two years.

sections.label: Singapore pandemic aid donations
sections.summary: Singapore donated medical supplies, including liquid oxygen and vaccine doses, to Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei and India.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I would add that we donated our entitlements to our neighbours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also responded quickly to urgent medical needs by sending medical supplies, including more than 500 tonnes of liquid oxygen to Indonesia through our "Oxygen Shuttle" programme and 120,000 vaccine doses to Batam and the Riau Islands, as well as 100,000 and 200,000 vaccine doses to Malaysia and Brunei respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also sent a consignment of 256 oxygen cylinders to support India's pandemic response at the height of its second wave last April.

sections.label: ASEAN and UN ceasefire diplomacy
sections.summary: Singapore works with ASEAN and UN neighbours, noting 141 countries voted for a UN resolution and ASEAN will issue a ceasefire statement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We make common cause with our neighbours and our friends, within ASEAN and in the UN General Assembly to the maximum extent possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, for instance, last night, there was an overwhelming vote – 141 countries at the UN General Assembly voted in favour of the resolution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In ASEAN, all our Ministers, I can tell you, were up until 1.00 am to 2.00 am last night communicating and we will shortly be issuing an ASEAN statement calling for an immediate ceasefire.

sections.label: China's international schemes
sections.summary: China promotes constructs like the Belt and Road Initiative and the Global Development Initiative to broaden and deepen relations with other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: China is promoting its own constructs to broaden and deepen its relations with other countries in the world through international schemes, such as the Belt and Road Initiative, and more recently, the Global Development Initiative.

sections.label: Resetting US-China postures
sections.summary: Moralistic or ideological disagreements on human rights or political systems cause deadlocks, so both countries should reset postures and reduce zero-sum competition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, disagreements cast in moralistic or ideological terms on issues like human rights or political systems quickly lead to deadlocks where no compromise is possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We hope both countries will accept that there is a need to reset their postures, to work out a new modus vivendi, and to reduce zero-sum competition.

sections.label: Engaging both powers diplomatically
sections.summary: Singapore engages both powers through diplomacy grounded in international law and peaceful dispute resolution, deciding by long-term national interests, not as a proxy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will continue to engage both powers through diplomacy grounded in fundamental principles, such as adherence to international law, the resolution of disputes by peaceful means, respect for sovereignty, the sanctity of borders and upholding a rules-based multilateral system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, we make decisions based on our long-term national interests and we make it clear to both that we will not be a proxy vassal state or a cat's paw for one side or the other.

sections.label: US TPP withdrawal mistake
sections.summary: The speaker told American interlocutors numerous times that it was a mistake for the US to pull out of the TPP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Quite frankly, I have told my American interlocutors on numerous occasions, it was a mistake for the US to pull out of the TPP.

sections.label: CPTPP accession applications
sections.summary: The UK, China and Taiwan are applying to join the CPTPP, and progress on this front should be watched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, let us watch how progress is made on this front.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And it is also no accident that now you have got the UK, China and Taiwan applying to join the CPTPP.

sections.label: Small states and multilateral order
sections.summary: Singapore works to strengthen the rules-based multilateral order and free trade through forums and agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Small states like Singapore value a system, where sovereign states, regardless of size, have equal rights and disputes can be settled peacefully in accordance with international law and agreed rules, and not to be subject to the rules of the jungle where might is right or to be forced to make invidious choices between big powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have spared no effort to strengthen the rules-based multilateral order so that it continues to provide us with a platform to safeguard our interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And that is why we worked with a cross-regional group of countries to establish the Forum of Small States, which, in fact, celebrates its 30th anniversary this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The rise of protectionism amidst COVID-19 has also underscored the importance of: one, upholding a free, open and rules-based multilateral trading system, as embodied by the WTO; second, deepening economic integration at multilateral fora, such as APEC and G20; third, diversifying trade relations through regional arrangements, such as the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) and our latest free trade agreement, the Pacific Alliance-Singapore Free Trade Agreement.

sections.label: Cybersecurity multilateral architecture
sections.summary: Singapore works with the international community and UN groups toward global cybersecurity governance principles and standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, in cybersecurity, which is a clear and present threat right now, we clearly need to work with the international community towards arriving at a global consensus, including through the creation of a multilateral architecture in cyberspace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are members of both the United Nations Open-Ended Working Group on Cybersecurity – in fact, this is chaired by Singapore 	– and the UN Group of Government Experts on Cybersecurity to foster understanding and collaboration on the development of new governance principles, frameworks and standards.

sections.label: UNCLOS 40th anniversary
sections.summary: Singapore affirms the primacy and universality of UNCLOS, which sets the legal framework for ocean activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Similarly, this year, I should also add, marks the 40th anniversary of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And amidst all the oceans-related challenges today, we continue to affirm the primacy and the universality of UNCLOS, which sets out the legal framework for all activities in the oceans.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia bilateral agreements
sections.summary: Singapore and Indonesia signed agreements on the Flight Information Region, defence cooperation and extradition of fugitives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Leaders' Retreat held in January marked a significant milestone in our bilateral relations and Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean delivered a Ministerial Statement last month explaining the significance of the agreements that Singapore and Indonesia signed to address longstanding bilateral issues, namely, the Flight Information Region, the defence cooperation and the extradition of fugitives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Flight Information Region (FIR) Agreement will uphold the safety and efficiency of air traffic in our region in a manner that is consistent with International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) rules and meet the civil aviation needs of both countries.

sections.label: Extradition Treaty cooperation
sections.summary: The Extradition Treaty enhances cooperation against crime, signals investors, and all agreements enter into force simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Extradition Treaty will enhance cooperation in combating crime and send a positive signal to investors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Both countries also exchanged letters to undertake that all these agreements will enter into force simultaneously.

sections.label: ASEAN Five-Point Consensus
sections.summary: ASEAN leaders met in April 2021 and arrived at the Five-Point Consensus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The ASEAN leaders had a meeting in April 2021 and arrived at the Five-Point Consensus.

sections.label: Malaysia supply and Iskandar committee
sections.summary: Singapore thanks Malaysian friends including truck drivers, and reaffirmed commitment to Iskandar Malaysia's manufacturing ecosystem at the 14th Joint Ministerial Committee on 21 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It has not been easy and we thank our Malaysian friends, including truck drivers who undergo regular testing to ensure that supplies reach us.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We convened with Malaysia the 14th Joint Ministerial Committee for Iskandar Malaysia on 21 December 2021, where we reaffirmed our commitment to strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem in Iskandar Malaysia.

sections.label: Vaccine and test kit donations
sections.summary: Singapore donated over 100,000 vaccine doses and over 100,000 test kits to Johor last year and engaged the state government on reopening the land border.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, we donated over 100,000 vaccine doses and over 100,000 test kits to Johor last year and have regularly engaged the state government on the re-opening of the Singapore-Johor land border.

sections.label: Singapore investments in 2021
sections.summary: In 2021, investments from Singapore reached US$9.4 billion despite the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2021, investments from Singapore reached US$9.4 billion despite the pandemic.

sections.label: Nongsa Digital Town launch
sections.summary: The Nongsa Digital Town was launched last year and is set to house 8,000 tech talents when completed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The Nongsa Digital Town was launched last year and is set to house 8,000 tech talents when completed.

sections.label: Moderna vaccines to Brunei
sections.summary: In September 2021, Singapore sent 100,000 doses of the Moderna vaccines to Brunei.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For instance, in September 2021, we sent 100,000 doses of the Moderna vaccines to Brunei.

sections.label: Haj resumption and quota
sections.summary: The Haj's resumption was discussed during the Prime Minister's recent phone call with the Saudi Crown Prince, where Prime Minister Lee requested an increased Haj quota.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I understand the eagerness of the community for the Haj to resume.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This was discussed during the Prime Minister’s recent phone call with the Saudi Crown Prince during which Prime Minister Lee requested for our Haj quota to be increased.

sections.label: MFA support for Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: MFA supports Palestinian Authority capacity building through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package, doubled to $10 million in 2016, benefiting over 600 Palestinian officials.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Mr Zhulkarnain sought an update on MFA's efforts to support capacity building in the Palestinian Authority (PA).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We continue to do so through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP) which we doubled from $5 million to $10 million in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The ETAP has benefited more than 600 Palestinian officials who have participated in courses, in areas, such as public administration, economic development and urban development.

sections.label: Singapore regional cooperation examples
sections.summary: MAS and Bank of Thailand linked PayNow and PromptPay in April 2021, and Singapore gave seed money for Philippines typhoon relief in December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, in April 2021, MAS and the Bank of Thailand launched the linkage of Singapore’s PayNow and Thailand’s PromptPay, the first of its kind in the world for cross-border real-time retail payment, which has brought convenience to users from both countries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: When Typhoon Rai struck the Philippines in December 2021, we contributed seed money to support the Singapore Red Cross' public fundraising for disaster relief and recovery efforts.

sections.label: ASEAN partnerships and summit
sections.summary: In 2021, ASEAN established Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships with China and Australia and held an ASEAN-China Special Summit in November.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2021, ASEAN established Comprehensive Strategic Partnerships with China and Australia and held an ASEAN-China Special Summit in November.

sections.label: Singapore with ASEAN Chair Cambodia
sections.summary: Singapore stands ready to work with ASEAN Chair Cambodia on community-building and regional economic integration, including implementing RCEP, in force since January 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore stands ready to work with the ASEAN Chair, Cambodia, to advance ASEAN’s community-building and regional economic integration efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: These include the implementation of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), which entered into force in January 2022.

sections.label: Singapore investment in India
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the largest foreign investors in India, with Direct Investment Abroad to India in 2020 at S$66.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore is one of the largest foreign investors in India, with our Direct Investment Abroad to India in 2020 standing at S$66.1 billion.

sections.label: Pacific Alliance-Singapore FTA signed
sections.summary: In January 2022, the Pacific Alliance-Singapore Free Trade Agreement was signed between Singapore, Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In January 2022, the Pacific Alliance-Singapore Free Trade Agreement, or PASFTA, was signed between Singapore, Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru.

sections.label: Singapore Cooperation Programme in South Pacific
sections.summary: Singapore shares development experience through the SCP, which has benefited 5,300 officials from the South Pacific region.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This will enable us to better contribute to the South Pacific’s development journey by sharing our development experience through the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Thus far, 5,300 officials from this region have benefited from our SCP.

sections.label: Singapore-China bilateral cooperation mechanisms
sections.summary: Singapore and China have close relations and cooperation mechanisms including the JCBC, eight provincial-level Economic and Trade councils, and three Government-to-Government projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Singapore and China have enjoyed close bilateral relations and established a wide range of cooperation mechanisms – the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC), the eight provincial-level Economic and Trade councils, and three Government-to-Government projects.

sections.label: 17th JCBC and China partnership
sections.summary: At the 17th JCBC, new cooperation areas were agreed, and discussions with Chinese leaders affirmed the 2015 All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: At the 17th JCBC last December, we agreed on new areas of bilateral cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Her friendly discussions with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Keqiang served to cement our bilateral relationship and affirmed the substantive, wide-ranging and forward-looking nature of our unique "All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times" established in 2015.

sections.label: Singapore as US security partner
sections.summary: Singapore is the US' only Major Security Cooperation Partner, showing the strength and depth of the relationship.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Singapore is the US’ only “Major Security Cooperation Partner”, demonstrating the strength and depth of the relationship.

sections.label: UK-Singapore Digital Economy Agreement
sections.summary: The UK-Singapore Digital Economy Agreement was signed, the first digital pact between an Asian and a European country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Another milestone was reached last week when we signed the UK-Singapore Digital Economy Agreement – the first digital pact between an Asian and a European country, and a pathfinder in setting high-standard digital trade rules between both regions.

sections.label: Singapore Cooperation Programme anniversary
sections.summary: The SCP, marking its 30th anniversary in 2022, has hosted about 137,000 foreign government officials over three decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) is our way of giving back to the international community, having benefited from similar assistance during our formative years. 2022 marks the SCP’s 30th anniversary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have hosted some 137,000 foreign government officials to our programmes over the past three decades.

sections.label: Sustainable development capacity-building efforts
sections.summary: Singapore contributes to the 2030 Agenda by focusing capacity-building on developing countries and small states, including the FOSS for Good package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This is part of our contribution to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We will continue to focus our capacity-building efforts on developing countries and small states, such as through the “FOSS for Good” technical assistance package, which was launched in conjunction with the 30th anniversary of the Forum of Small States (FOSS) this year.

sections.label: Singaporeans stranded in Malaysia
sections.summary: MFA has assisted the return of over 450 Singaporeans stranded in Malaysia since March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Nearer home, MFA has assisted the return of over 450 Singaporeans stranded in Malaysia since March 2020.

sections.label: Death and Critical Illness scheme
sections.summary: Singapore launched the Death and Critical Illness Emergency Visits scheme with Malaysia last May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For instance, Singapore launched the Death and Critical Illness Emergency Visits (DCEV) scheme with Malaysia last May.

sections.label: Consular support and Ukraine announcements
sections.summary: MFA will strengthen consular support, while specific announcements on Ukraine and blocking Russian aircraft are still being worked out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: MFA will also strengthen our consular support of Singaporeans during this pandemic period and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: He mentioned earlier on in his speech that the specific announcements with regard to Ukraine, in terms of how Singapore will respond in terms of embargoes, were still being worked out.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But I wonder if he could elaborate on whether Singapore has plans to block Russian airlines and private aircraft from Russia from landing at Changi.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I am not in a position to make specific announcements yet.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, we will do so in due time.
